final.label: missing-explanation-at-declaration

skill_entry.name: 14. Explanation at the declaration: a new parameter, environment variable, routine, test-only helper, moved default or term must be explained where a reader meets it
skill_entry.trigger: (a) New parameter with a default or hedge-word name, absent from the leading comment at HEAD, hedge-named or never left at its default by any caller. (b) New getenv("VAR") read, absent at BASE, named nowhere else at HEAD. (c) New 20+ line function, absent at BASE, no comment above it; or an uncommented new t/ file. (d) Touched header function with only t/ callers, forwarding a parameter every production callee call passes as one constant, doc block silent. (e) src/ definition drops a default kept in the header, comment silent. (f) Design-spec prose introduces a quoted or bold term at first occurrence, no glossary row, link or gloss. (g) Prose demotes a document ('superseded', 'legacy') without deletion or retirement plan.
skill_entry.procedure: 1 Parameters: grep added defaulted parameters; grep the leading comment at HEAD for the name; hedge-word check; read callers' arguments. 2 Env vars: grep added getenv reads; drop ones read at BASE; grep HEAD for another mention. 3 Routines: `+` definitions absent at BASE, uncommented; brace-count bodies; fire once per PR, largest, nit. 4 Test-only helpers: classify callers of touched header functions; for an all-t/ helper read its `return CALLEE(` line and what production passes there. 5 Moved defaults: pair `-`/`+` definition lines; confirm the header holds it; grep the definition comment. 6 Terms: first occurrence versus hunk line, glossary, doc-tree link. 7 Superseded documents: grep the status section for a retirement plan. 8 One finding per candidate, at the declaration.
skill_entry.question: If a reader opens only this file at HEAD, can they learn what the new thing is for, when it applies and why it has this shape (why a 'hint', why a parameter production never varies, what the variable's format and default are, where the term is defined), without opening the PR thread?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A plain bug fix needs no Note; the ask is a short comment, never a Note (3866668853 questioned one). A parameter the doc block already covers. A plain-named defaulted parameter some caller leaves at its default (tron-4353 q_begin, q_end). A getenv read named by a comment, assertion message or log line (tron-4353, tron-2475). A moved, renamed or converted function; a self-describing member (debug_string); helpers under 20 lines, lambdas, fixtures. A test-only helper whose callee takes a variable in production (xfer_v_entry, silent in PR 4007 and tron-3756). Zero-caller symbols: dead-symbol check. A dereferenced hedge-word parameter: identifier-name check. An env var no wrapper forwards: observability check. A stale comment: comment-contradicts-code. README, comment and shell-help terms (tron-1727). Document structure, renames, comment-only PRs.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Code: "can we document `<name>` (e.g. why is it a '<hedge word>' / why it keeps `<param>` when production always passes `<CONSTANT>` / how to use `<VAR>`, its format and default)? a reader of <file> alone cannot tell; a short comment at <the declaration | definition | read> would do." Test-only helper: "this `<helper>` is a UT-only utility function (only caller t/<file>:<line>). We should document that clearly, as well as the fact that it purposely uses `<param>` rather than `<CONSTANT>`." Prose: "first mention of '<term>'... is there a link/reference pointer to where this is better described (e.g. how it's enabled/disabled/driven)?" Document: "what is our retirement plan for <older doc>? It's confusing to come across multiple specs in multiple locations."
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit when he says so himself: 'I know this is a pretty simple routine, but I'm a fan of comments :)' (3036997452), 'kinda pedantic' (2789826297). minor is the default: a lowercase question with one reason ('can we document `kv_hint` (e.g. why is it a 'hint' :-p)?', ''erased'?'), and approval is not withheld (docs-51 approved three minutes after the ask, 16:54:17Z to 16:57:13Z on 2026-08-25; PR 2302 approved 37 seconds after the ask, 3036997452 at 15:32:55Z, APPROVED at 15:33:32Z on 2026-04-05). normal only for the retirement-plan case, where the reason is the cost to newcomers ('It's confusing (esp. for newer folks)'). Never blocking; he approved every member PR.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk + full file at HEAD (the leading comment block, the glossary section, the status or roadmap section) + callers (`git grep` over h src t bin ingest at HEAD, classified production versus t/) + BASE (is the function, variable or parameter new) + other files (the header declaration for a moved default; README and doc/ for an environment variable; the callee's production callers for a forwarded parameter) + prior PR and branches for a superseded document (`gh api .../branches`, open PRs). PR body only to confirm a documented claim (PR 4007 body: 'Two helpers / carry doc comments answering questions raised in review', split over a line break). Not commits, not CI, not runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: explanation at the declaration

Common setup additions (apply to every check): for a review commit already merged, `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself and pr.diff is empty. Use the first-parent main commit that is an ancestor of HEAD: `for c in $(git -C WT log --first-parent --format=%H -n 400 origin/main); do git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor $c HEAD && { BASE=$c; break; }; done` (PR 4007 at 29a39ac33e: BASE 21162f5568, pr.diff 282 lines, 4 files). The installed awk is mawk 1.3.4, which has no `\s`; write `[[:space:]]` in every awk and grep pattern.

Trigger detail. (a) A `+` line inside a parameter list (previous diff line of the hunk ends with `,` or `(`) that carries a default value or a hedge word in the name (hint, tmp, temp, opt, maybe, hack); the function's leading comment block at HEAD does not name the parameter; and either the name carries a hedge word or no caller at HEAD under h, src or t leaves the argument at its default. (b) A `+` line reads getenv("VAR") where no `-` line of the same hunk reads VAR and no file at BASE reads it, and `git grep -w VAR HEAD` finds no comment, README, doc, log-format string or assertion message naming VAR outside the read. (c) A function definition of 20 or more lines (brace-depth count) whose definition line is a `+` line, whose name and first body line are absent at BASE (not moved, renamed or converted from a TEST_CASE), and whose nearest preceding line that is not blank, a `#` directive, a `template <...>` line or an attribute macro (`TRON(...)`, `[[...]]`) is not a comment; or a new file under t/ with zero `//` lines. (d) The diff adds a header function, or changes a parameter it forwards, whose every call site outside its own definition and doc block is under t/, and the helper forwards a parameter to a callee that every production caller under h or src passes as one named constant, and the doc block neither says test-only, UT-only or not production nor names that constant. (e) A definition in src/ drops a default (`-` line with `= value`, `+` line and continuation lines without) because the default now lives in the header declaration, and the doc comment above the definition does not state the default. (f) A prose hunk in a design specification (docs/ or doc/ of a specification repository, or a tron doc/ design note) introduces a quoted, bold or capitalised term whose first occurrence in the file at HEAD is inside the hunk, with no glossary row, link or parenthetical definition before or at that line. (g) A prose hunk says an existing document 'is no longer the authority', 'remain(s)', 'superseded', 'deprecated' or 'legacy' and neither deletes it nor turns it into a pointer nor states a retirement plan.

1. Parameters: `grep -n -E '^\+[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ [A-Za-z_0-9]+ = [^,;()]+(,|\)[^;{]*\{)$' pr.diff`; keep a hit only when the previous diff line of the same hunk ends with `,` or `(` (inside a parameter list); do not exclude by type name (`size_t q_begin = 0,` is a parameter); discard shell lines (`exit 2`, `shift 2`) and `struct X {`. Map each to FILE:LINE through the `@@` headers. Leading comment block: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | head -n $((LINE-1)) | tac | awk '/^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/ {print; next} NF {exit}' | tac | grep -c NAME` (0 = candidate). Hedge word: `echo NAME | grep -E 'hint|tmp|temp|opt|maybe|hack'`. Use in the body: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E "\bNAME\b"` (an `if (NAME &&` guard means optional; `->` or `*NAME` means required). Callers: `git -C WT grep -n -A6 'FUNCTION(' HEAD -- h src t | grep -v "FILE:LINE"`; read the argument in that position at each call; drop the hit when the name has no hedge word and at least one caller omits the argument.
2. Environment variables: `grep -n -E '^\+.*getenv\("([A-Z0-9_]+)"' pr.diff`; drop VAR when a `-` line of the same hunk reads it (re-spelled read) or `git -C WT grep -c 'getenv("VAR")' BASE -- h src t bin` hits a file other than FILE (pre-existing variable; PR 2302 TRON_LOG_LEVEL). Then `git -C WT grep -n -w VAR HEAD -- README*.md doc h src t bin | grep -v 'getenv("VAR")'` (0 hits = candidate; a comment, a log-format string or an assertion message counts as a mention). Record the parse at the read line (`stoul(..., 0)` = any base, default value, bound).
3. Uncommented routines: `for f in $(grep -E '^(h|src|t)/' prfiles.txt); do git -C WT show HEAD:$f | awk -v F=$f '/^(static |inline |template)?[A-Za-z_:<>*&, ]+ [A-Za-z_0-9:]+\(.*\)[^;]*\{$/ && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*:/ && prev !~ /^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*|\*\/|\/\*)/ {print F":"NR": "$0} {if ($0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*$/ && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*(TRON\(|template[[:space:]]*<|\[\[|#)/) prev=$0}'; done` (constructor initializer lines and attribute, template and directive lines are skipped). Keep a hit only when its definition line is a `+` line in pr.diff, the name is absent at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -c 'NAME('` = 0), the signature is on no `-` line of pr.diff, and the first body line is absent at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -c -F 'FIRST_BODY_LINE'` = 0; this removes moves and TEST_CASE conversions). Body length by brace count: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR>=L {n++; d+=gsub(/\{/,"{"); d-=gsub(/\}/,"}"); if (d>0) seen=1; if (seen && d==0) {print n; exit}}'` (keep >= 20). New file: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -c '^[[:space:]]*//'` (0 = no comment in the file). Fire once per PR on the largest; nit.
4. Test-only header functions: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} /^@@/ && f ~ /^a\/h\// {print f": "$0}' pr.diff | sed 's/@@.*@@//' | sort -u`; drop context lines that start with struct, class, public:, private:, static const or contain `=`. For a hunk whose context is a struct, scan upward from the hunk's new-side start line for the nearest member signature: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v S=START 'NR<=S && /^  [A-Za-z_].*\) *(const)? *(noexcept)? *\{$/ {n=NR; s=$0} END {print n": "s}'` (k_hwcacheblock::xfer for the :461 hunk on PR 4007). Per NAME: `git -C WT grep -n -E "\bNAME\(" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v -E "HEADER:(DEFLINE|DOCLINE)"`; all remaining hits under t/ = test-only; zero hits outside the function's own file = dead code, record for the dead-symbol check (3866653656 'dead file'), do not fire here. Doc block: `git -C WT show HEAD:HEADER | sed -n 'DOCSTART,DEFLINEp' | grep -E '\b(UT|[Tt]est|[Tt]est-only|[Pp]roduction)\b'` (no `-i`; `-i` on UT matches input, output, without). Forwarded call: `git -C WT show HEAD:HEADER | sed -n 'DEFLINE,/^}/p' | grep -n -E 'return [A-Za-z_]+\('` gives CALLEE and the forwarded argument list; `git -C WT grep -n -A3 'CALLEE(' HEAD -- h src` lists production calls; read the argument in each forwarded position by hand. Fire only when every production call passes one named constant in a forwarded position (PR 4007: HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE from k_hwcacheblock::xfer). Otherwise pass silently (xfer_v_entry at 29a39ac33e and 7206e88cc2: callee shuffle_v_entry takes kv_head_size at production calls :598/:619 and :620/:641). Never report a sibling helper Wade passed as a second finding.
5. Moved defaults: `grep -n -E '^-[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ [A-Za-z_0-9]+ = (nullptr|false|true|0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+)\)? *(noexcept)? *\{' pr.diff` (a typed parameter line, not an `if` or `for` line); keep a hit only when the paired `+` line and its continuation lines carry no `=` default and `git -C WT grep -n -A8 'FUNCTION(' HEAD -- h` shows the default in the header declaration. Definition comment: the step 1 tac/awk block over SRCFILE at DEFLINE piped to `grep -i -E 'default|OPTIONAL'` (0 = candidate). Remedy = a comment line at the definition (C++ allows a default argument once per scope); nit.
6. Terms: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} (f ~ /\.(md|txt)$/ || /^\+[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*)/) && /^\+/' pr.diff | grep -E "(^|[ (])'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z -]+'([ ,.)]|$)|\*\*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z /-]+\*\*"`; skip a line whose quotes are possessives (`'s `). Only files under docs/ or doc/ of a specification repository, or a tron doc/ design note, count; README usage notes, code comments and shell help text do not. Per TERM: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -i -w "TERM" | head -3` (first occurrence versus hunk line); `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -i '^#.*gloss'` then grep that range for TERM; `git -C WT grep -n -i -l "TERM" HEAD -- doc docs README*.md`. First occurrence in the hunk, no glossary row, no link = candidate. For a repository outside WT: `gh api "repos/ORG/REPO/contents/PATH?ref=HEAD" --jq .content | base64 -d > spec.md` and run the same greps on spec.md.
7. Superseded documents: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} (f ~ /\.md$/ || f ~ /\/doc/ || /^\+[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*)/) && /^\+/' pr.diff | grep -n -i -E 'no longer (the )?(stated )?authority|superseded|deprecated|legacy|remain(s)? (on|in|but)|older (doc|spec|model)'`; an identifier such as `legacy_attention_storage_schedule()` does not count. Per document: `git -C WT ls-files DOC`; `gh api repos/ORG/REPO/branches --jq '.[].name'` for branch-only drafts; `gh pr list --repo ORG/REPO --search DOC`; then `grep -n -i -E 'retire|tombstone|delete|remove|close(s)? (PR|#)' spec.md` inside the status or roadmap section (0 = candidate).
8. One finding per candidate, phrased as a question at the declaration line, the read, the definition or the first use; remedy = comment, @param line, glossary row, link or roadmap row. Never a Note, never a code change.

On PR 4007 at 29a39ac33e (BASE 21162f5568 by the first-parent recipe; pr.diff 282 lines, 4 files): steps 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 = 0 hits (the only getenv is USE_HW_ATTN on a context line, pr4007.diff:339); step 3: 11 raw hits with `[[:space:]]`, one `+` definition (t/t_hwattention_batch.cpp:56 hwattn_batch_case, 279 lines, commented at :53-54 above its template line, dropped); step 4 lists xfer_k_entry, xfer_k_packed_entry and dump_k_cache_from_hbm (4 hits, all inside h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp, routed to the dead-symbol check) plus two struct context lines; xfer_k_entry (:1023) callers outside the doc mention :962 and the definition = t/t_hwattention.cpp:418 only; doc block :1003-1022 has no test, UT or production word; callee xfer_k_packed_entry (:977) is called by production k_hwcacheblock::xfer (src/pos/hwattention.cpp:26) with HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE while the test passes head_size (:419) = fired (3866590750, 3866568650). xfer_v_entry (:1072; caller t/:422; callee shuffle_v_entry production calls :598/:619 pass kv_head_size) = not fired, matching Wade's silence. Closed at 3a8544cd35 by :1062-1067 ('Test-only helper ... deliberately forwards the caller's `head_size`') and the @param head_size paragraph :1022-1027.
On PR 2176: the step 1 regex over `gh pr diff 2176` returns 4 hits: :2182 `tron::node_base* kv_hint = nullptr) {` plus three undefaulted `hbm_address_t v_base) {` / `hbm_address_t& v_base) {` lines (:2905, :3021, :3801) dropped for carrying neither a default nor a hedge word; leading comment 429249ead6:h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:742-745 names skip_compare only; body guards `if (kv_hint && hardware::gof_configured())` at :789; both callers :922 and :963 pass flush_hint, none uses the default = fired (2948108341).
On PR 2302 (commits 8a433ff19e, d39c222fa8 on c09bf4004e; `git diff -U0 d39c222fa8~2 d39c222fa8`): step 2 hits TRON_LOG_LEVEL (pr line 132; read at BASE by src/system/spdlog.cpp:34 and four test files, dropped as pre-existing) and TRON_POISON_BITS (t/t_clearhbm.cpp:71 at d39c222fa8, std::stoul base 0, default 0, no other mention in the tree); step 3: device_thread :35-67 (33 lines, definition at pr line 142), the file has 0 `//` lines = fired once as a nit (3036997452).

Silent calibration (15 of the 48 silent diffs probed): step 1 regex = 5 non-parameter hits (tron-1727.diff:74,77,83,89 shell lines; tron-4353.diff:282 `struct candidate {`), 0 parameters; the literal trigger would hit tron-4353 q_begin/q_end (h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1385-1386 at a9a9cf30a4, doc block :1320-1373 names neither), removed by the caller rule (production :1116-1118 passes section.q_begin/q_end, nine test callers omit them). final.widen_delta: New check, no existing check widened. SKILL.md: append question 14 to the numbered list ("Declaration: if a reader opens only this file at HEAD, can they learn what the new parameter, variable, routine, helper, default or term is for and why it has this shape?"); add section "### 14. Explanation at the declaration" with the trigger (a)-(g), procedure, do-not-fire and finding shapes above, under a new heading "Checks on explanations" after check 13; add to Words used here: getenv (the C library read of an environment variable), @param (the doxygen parameter tag), UT (unit test), hedge word (hint, tmp, temp, opt, maybe, hack in a name), brace count (body length measured to the brace that closes the definition); extend the frontmatter description with "new parameters, environment variables, helpers and terms with no explanation where a reader meets them". procedures.md: add "## Check 14" with the eight commands, the trigger detail, the six On-PR lines and the silent-calibration line; add to Common setup the first-parent BASE recipe for merged review commits and the mawk note (`[[:space:]]`, never `\s`), both of which apply to every check. Cross-references: a stale comment stays with comment-contradicts-adjacent-code (2789661703); a Note request on a bug fix is a do-not-fire here and belongs to code-comment-carries-no-lasting-fact (3866668853); a zero-caller function goes to dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition; a hedge-word parameter the body dereferences goes to identifier-name-states-role; an environment variable no launcher wrapper forwards goes to observability-and-operability-of-new-path (5106398334). "How Wade words a finding" gains one bullet: the remedy for a missing explanation is a comment line, a @param line, a glossary row or a link, never a Note and never a code change.

final.precedent_note: n = 8 comments over 6 PRs (tron-2011, tron-2176, tron-2302, tron-4007, asimovsw-docs-51, asimovsw-docs-64), 2026-02-10 to 2026-09-24. No member is pasted assistant text: the nine pasted texts sit in PRs 2233, 2461, 2872, 2906, 3008, 3490, 4128, 3879 and 4191, none of which is a member PR. One member (3866568650) is Wade's reply to another reviewer's question, not a top-level comment. The do-not-fire quote 3866668853 is not a member. Wade approved every member PR (2011 at d4795f37a5, 2176 at 8e19ea3e62, 2302 at d39c222fa8, 4007 at 3a8544cd35, docs-51 at e83e9e99e4, docs-64 at 3b1f9ae87b). Two of the eight (the term and retirement asks) come from one specification repository, one author, 2026-08/09.
changes_made: Trigger (a) narrowed per PRECISION: a defaulted parameter with a plain name fires only when no caller leaves it at its default; tron-4353 q_begin/q_end (silent, nine test callers omit them) no longer fires. Step 1 regex rewritten to match any typed parameter with a default, not excluded by type name, with the inside-a-parameter-list rule and the non-parameter discards (shell lines, struct openers).

Trigger (b) and step 2 aligned (PRECISION and FACTS): a log-format string or assertion message counts as a mention; a `-` line in the same hunk or a getenv of the same VAR elsewhere at BASE drops the hit. On-PR-2302 line now records TRON_LOG_LEVEL (pr line 132, pre-existing, dropped) next to TRON_POISON_BITS.

Trigger (c) and step 3 rewritten (PRECISION and EXECUTABILITY): new-function test (name and first body line absent at BASE, signature on no `-` line) removes moves (tron-1707 debug_wtdump), renames (tron-3756 debug_exit) and TEST_CASE conversions (tron-4353); preceding-line rule skips blank, directive, template and attribute-macro lines (hwattn_batch_case, init_attn_section_split_cap, is_kv_complete no longer listed); constructor initializer lines excluded; body length by brace count instead of first column-0 brace; self-describing member names (debug_string) exempt.

Trigger (d) and step 4: adopted PRECISION's forwarded-constant requirement over EXECUTABILITY's fold-into-sibling remedy. Decided by re-reading the code: at 29a39ac33e xfer_v_entry's callers are its definition :1072 and t/t_hwattention.cpp:422, and its callee shuffle_v_entry is called by production at :598 and :619 with kv_head_size (a variable); Wade was silent on it in PR 4007 and tron-3756, so the check must not fire on it at all, which makes the sibling rule unnecessary. Kept EXECUTABILITY's point as the sentence 'Never report a sibling helper Wade passed as a second finding'. Added the struct-context member lookup, the case-sensitive doc-block grep (no -i on UT), the `return CALLEE(` command for the forwarded call, and the zero-caller route to the dead-symbol check.
Step 5 regex restricted to typed parameter lines and to pairs where the `+` line and its continuation lines drop the default (tron-3756 make_stub_device and tron-4353 pending no longer hit).
